decode.scroll_stop_trick: Two round bellies in profile almost touching — a pregnant woman's and a man's — and the only line on the image is 'Only one of them is pregnant.' The joke lands before the brand does.
decode.angle_carried: beer belly (A1) — pure visual joke, almost no text (Adrien Loom 2: 'pure visual joke, good')
decode.hidden_reading: his belly is as round as hers and has no excuse — shame disguised as a joke, then relief: it isn't what he thinks
decode.scene_logic: a profile shot of two bellies side by side, same height, same roundness; ours identical: the pregnant woman in a white cardigan and bra top, the man in an open white shirt and jeans, hands in pockets
decode.visual_trick: symmetry of two bellies that mean opposite things; copy literally
decode.shape_or_function_equivalent: none needed — the man's belly is our A8-M subject as is; the product only appears as a small pouch
decode.render_style: photoreal, neutral grey studio backdrop, soft flat light, slightly warm skin
decode.text_treatment: one line, bold white sans with a dark drop shadow, top of the image; nothing else

strategy.angle: A8-M the man's belly that isn't fat — he blames the beer, it's fluid
strategy.mechanism: M1: when the body can't clear everyday oxidative stress, the tissue in the legs stays inflamed and stops draining normally, so fluid sits there — heavy, tender, puffy — and no diet reaches it, because it was never fat; the tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, reaches the tissue and helps the body switch that process off so normal drainage can resume
strategy.sub_avatar: trigger: his wife's joke, the belt notch · cause: inflamed tissue holding fluid, not beer · tried: skipping beer, sit-ups, 'eating clean'
strategy.belief_installed: A belly that no diet moves isn't food I stored — it's what my body stopped clearing.
